key_insight: A simple deletion-based atom extraction strategy gives the most reliable small periodic DFT-ready environments for training interatomic potentials from large-scale simulations.
engineering_relevance: This helps active-learning and on-the-fly potential development by making it easier to generate accurate, compact reference calculations from very large atomistic systems.
method: Benchmark multiple ways to carve out local atomic environments from bulk simulations for periodic DFT.
Compare shape/size choices and the use of passivating envelopes for extracted clusters.
Test on diverse materials: amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark across multiple material classes, and the deletion method outperformed alternative extraction approaches.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the extracted region and any boundary passivation preserve the local physics needed for DFT accuracy.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
